title: A semantic key preserves propositions across alternate readings
summary: A latent transcription-channel model first assigns alternate reading uncertainty, then infers a small semantic key whose proposition is invariant across ZL3b, IT2a and RF1b readings.

design.mechanism: one proposition invariant across readings versus a reading-conditioned semantic code
design.unit: held complete constructions or paired reading contexts
design.contrast: After marginalizing reading uncertainty, held paraphrase/role commitments should agree across all three readings; a reading-conditioned code predicts systematic proposition changes tied to the edition.
design.prediction: Old reading-fidelity and latent-channel work tested surface prediction or transcription policy, not a held semantic invariant with a rival reading-conditioned meaning.
design.countermodel: A surface-copying, renderer, or context-conditioned convention can mimic training observations without the proposed semantic mechanism.
design.falsifier: A held family requires different semantic propositions by reading despite equal source context, or the invariant model only succeeds through renderer labels.
design.principal_risk: Need cached alternate readings and independently defined proposition constraints; no English gold is available.
design.smallest_test: Fit on two reading-stable construction families, hold one family out, and compare invariant versus reading-conditioned predictions.
design.prior_duplicate_pointers: Near GDT832 and LTG001; distinct target is semantic proposition invariance, not transcription accuracy.
design.selection_status: raw unreviewed; no readiness or novelty claim
